ideas.title: I throw too hard
ideas.critique: Lumi doing a comic physical thing to Pinchy follows straight on from the jelly ball. But real orbits that keep their speed and slowly spread into a ring are physics the island never had, and the ring grows all day, so there is something new to look up at every time. The flyby every forty seconds is the hook people would come back for, as long as the orbit is really simulated and not a scripted loop.

ideas.title: The black marble
ideas.critique: Everything pulled to one point and heaping up is the payoff of the rope tangle again, and a pumpkin falling in is easy to guess. The player choosing where the pull is, plants and friends bending under one inverse-square field, and everything springing back are new and can be played. The lensing ring is the strongest light idea in the round if the glass shell really bends the island into a ring and doesn't just blur it.

ideas.title: Toasting Marshmallow
ideas.critique: Burning things is an example the human's goals name, and a hot dot that friends jump away from is close to the pointer that friends react to. The true caustic from a glass lens is real path tracer work, and scorch marks that stay give the meadow a memory, but the friend's bottom and the popping pumpkin are the gags everyone will expect.

ideas.title: Spin echo, by lamplight
ideas.critique: This is round 1's spin echo again, with the risk it had: from above it is the crowd under one rule. The light pools fix the weakness the critic named, because dephasing and refocusing become sweeping beams that meet on one spot, and timing the second clap gives the player a real job. It only works if the beams visibly come back together without any scripting.

ideas.title: The ground turns to honey
ideas.critique: Turning the whole meadow into something else for a minute is the flood, the sand dunes and the slow-motion zones again: friends wading slowly and a building that leans are the expected beats. The glossy amber subsurface material and friends staying stuck until dug out are the only parts with something to come back to.

ideas.title: Sonar in the dark
ideas.critique: Hide and seek is a familiar game, and friends shouting back is a speech gag the island has done often. Seeing the island only where expanding shells of light pass is a new way to look at it: the rings crossing in the dark make a picture of their own and give a real reason to play another round.

ideas.title: The island under glass, shaken
ideas.critique: This is round 1's snow globe reworded: shaking the world so the friends slide is still the tilt game in a new frame, and sloshing water is an example the human named. The nose prints that stay on the glass are a small new detail. The real glass and the snow you whip up with your hand are still the strong part.
